rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a clean, minimal baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: one modality, one profile, a standard linear encoder, and no aggregation or fusion. This gives a well-defined reference accuracy for the RNA modality. In subsequent experiments I can then test image-only (config_010), compare RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), and evaluate whether multimodal fusion adds value over the best single modality. Starting with the simplest baseline avoids confounding multiple design choices and provides the most interpretable anchor point for the 9 remaining experiments.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only 48.5% accuracy, suggesting the linear PCA representation may be a significant bottleneck. Question: Does a learned nonlinear RNA encoder (scvi_n200) substantially improve over PCA while holding all other factors constant (same model setting, profile setting, no image)? This is a clean single-variable A/B comparison that isolates the encoder effect. Why this is the best next experiment: With 8 experiments remaining, I need to determine whether the RNA representation is the primary limitation before investing budget in multimodal or multiprofile configurations. If scvi_n200 shows a large jump, it validates investing in richer encoders (scgpt) and justifies pairing them with image later. If it shows little change, it signals that RNA signal is inherently limited and I should pivot toward image-only or multimodal configs. This controlled comparison maximizes information per experiment under the tight budget.

Evidence: config_004 (scvi_n200, singleprofile, RNA-only) achieved 0.5203 accuracy vs config_001 (pca_n2000) at 0.4849, suggesting a learned biological encoder is preferable. However, we have zero information about whether image features carry useful signal for this task. This experiment (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) establishes the image-modality baseline, which is the most critical unknown for allocating the remaining 7 experiments. If image-only performs comparably or better than RNA-only, multimodal fusion configurations become high-priority; if it performs poorly, we should focus remaining budget on RNA-only improvements (multiprofile, scgpt encoder). This single clean test reduces the largest source of uncertainty in the search space without confounding multiple design choices.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (0.520) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.485) in the simplest rna_only/singleprofile setting, and image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.208), confirming RNA as the dominant signal. Uncertainty: we have not yet tested the scgpt encoder, which may capture richer transcriptomic representations than either PCA or scVI. This experiment (config_007: rna_only, singleprofile, scgpt) isolates exactly one variable—RNA encoder—against the two already tested, giving a clean three-way comparison. Knowing the best RNA encoder before investing remaining budget in multiprofile aggregation, image modality, and multimodal fusion is critical: it ensures all downstream experiments build on the strongest single-modality baseline, avoiding wasted experiments on suboptimal encoders. With 7 experiments remaining, this foundational comparison is the highest-information next step.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (config_004: acc=0.520), and all tested models are singleprofile. The image modality is very weak (resnet50: 0.208), so the immediate question is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve the already-strong RNA signal. This experiment (config_005: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean single-variable extension of config_004, isolating the effect of multiprofile + avgpool aggregation. If it improves over 0.520, it validates the multiprofile direction and justifies further investment in aggregation/fusion choices; if not, it frees remaining budget to explore multimodal or alternative encoders. With 5 experiments left, resolving the profile-setting question with the best encoder is the highest-information next step.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over its singleprofile counterpart config_004 (0.520). Among RNA encoders, scvi_n200 consistently outperforms pca_n2000 and scgpt. The key untested variable in this promising direction is the aggregation method: avgpool vs. transformer. config_006 isolates exactly this comparison by keeping everything identical to config_005 except switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer. This is the highest-value next experiment because (1) it exploits the clearly dominant scvi_n200 + multiprofile direction, (2) it tests a single design change to cleanly attribute any performance difference to aggregation, and (3) if transformer aggregation helps, it sets up a stronger base for subsequent multimodal experiments in the remaining 4 budget slots. If it does not help, we confirm avgpool is sufficient and can pivot to multimodal exploration with confidence.

The current best is config_006 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, transformer) at 0.653 accuracy. The key remaining question is whether adding image features to this strong RNA baseline can push accuracy higher. Image-only is weak (0.208), but complementary information in multimodal fusion is not guaranteed to be absent. Config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) is the most direct extension of our best result, isolating the effect of adding the image modality while keeping the proven RNA encoder, multiprofile setting, and transformer aggregation. Weighted fusion is preferred over concat because the image modality is substantially weaker, and weighted fusion allows the model to downweight the less informative signal. This is the highest-value experiment: if it beats 0.653, we have a new best and a direction to refine; if it doesn't, we confirm RNA-only multiprofile is the ceiling and can spend remaining budget on minor refinements.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 accuracy. The image modality contributed ~6 points over RNA-only multiprofile, but image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image encoder may be underutilized. config_039 isolates a single variable—replacing resnet50 with the stronger imagenet_vit_l—while keeping the proven scvi_n200 encoder, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This tests whether a more powerful image representation can further amplify the multimodal gain. It is the highest-upside single-variable extension of the current best, and with only 2 experiments remaining, focusing on the most impactful design axis (image encoder quality) is the best use of this slot.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. All top-performing configs share the same backbone (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + multiprofile), but we have only tested 'weighted' fusion in the multimodal setting. config_038 isolates the fusion method by switching to 'concat' while holding every other parameter at its best-known value. This is a single-variable comparison that directly tests whether concatenating the two modality representations preserves more discriminative information than the weighted combination. It is the best use of experiment 9 because it probes the most important unexplored design dimension (fusion) on the strongest backbone, and the result will inform the final experiment: if concat wins, we can try a further refinement; if weighted wins, we confirm the current best and can spend the last experiment on a secondary axis (e.g., avgpool vs. transformer aggregation).

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI_n200, ViT-L, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. All major design axes (RNA encoder, profile, image encoder, fusion) are well-supported by evidence: scVI_n200 > PCA > scGPT, multiprofile >> single-profile, ViT-L > ResNet50, weighted > concat. The one remaining untested degree of freedom in this top-performing setup is aggregation: in RNA-only multiprofile, transformer (0.6530) edged out avgpool (0.6501) by a small margin (~0.003). Config_037 (same as config_039 but with avgpool instead of transformer) isolates whether that small aggregation preference holds in the multimodal ViT-L context. As the final experiment, this is the most logical exploitation step: it directly probes the closest untested variant of the best configuration, and if avgpool performs comparably or (unlikely) better, it would either confirm the robustness of the current best or reveal a new top result. No other untested config combines all the empirically superior choices, making this the highest-value last test.
